title: Agriculture in India: Crops, Seasons, and Farming Systems

questions.question: The zaid cropping season in India runs during which months?
questions.rationale: Zaid is the short summer season between rabi harvest and kharif sowing, irrigated and used for watermelons, cucumbers, vegetables, and fodder.

questions.question: Wheat in India is chiefly a crop of which season?
questions.rationale: Wheat is sown in October-November, grows through the cool winter, and is harvested in March-April, which makes it a rabi crop.

questions.question: Which temperature range suits wheat best at the ripening stage?
questions.rationale: Wheat needs about 10-15 degrees C while growing but warmer 21-26 degrees C weather for ripening; too much heat shrivels the grain.

questions.question: Cotton in India grows best on which type of soil?
questions.rationale: Black regur soil of the Deccan retains moisture and is formed from lava, which is why Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Telangana lead cotton output.

questions.question: Which state produces most of India's jute, the 'golden fibre'?
questions.rationale: The hot, humid Ganga-Brahmaputra delta of West Bengal provides loamy alluvium, water for retting, and cheap labour ideal for jute.

questions.question: Ragi, a hardy nutri-cereal, is grown mainly in which state?
questions.rationale: Ragi is concentrated in the dry southern interior, with Karnataka the leading producer; jowar leads in Maharashtra and bajra in Rajasthan.

questions.question: The Green Revolution of the mid-1960s was built on which package of inputs?
options: HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, and assured irrigation
questions.rationale: High-yielding varieties of wheat and rice combined with fertilisers, irrigation, and price support converted India from food importer to self-sufficiency.

questions.question: The White Revolution is associated with which programme and personality?
options: Fisheries missions led by M. S. Swaminathan
Operation Flood of 1970, led by Verghese Kurien
questions.rationale: Operation Flood, launched in 1970 with Anand in Gujarat as its base, made India the world's largest milk producer under Verghese Kurien.

questions.question: What is the approximate average size of an agricultural land holding in India?
questions.rationale: Successive agriculture censuses show the average holding falling to roughly 1.1 hectares, which limits mechanisation and bargaining power.

questions.question: According to recent foodgrain production figures, which crop contributes the most million tonnes?
questions.rationale: Rice at roughly 136 million tonnes tops the foodgrain basket, ahead of wheat at about 111 million tonnes.
